article.title: Why “Per Customer” Can Change the Story
article.why: Practical analytical English with higher-difficulty emphasis.

paragraphs.en:
A business report may say that spending per customer increased, but the phrase “per customer” is not complete until we know which customers are in the denominator. Imagine a store with 10,000 registered members, 4,000 active customers, and 2,000 people who actually purchased this month. If total monthly sales are $200,000, sales per registered member are $20, sales per active customer are $50, and sales per purchaser are $100. The same sales total creates three very different numbers.

None of these metrics is automatically wrong. Each answers a different question. Sales per registered member may be useful when the business wants to understand the value of its entire member base. Sales per active customer can help evaluate engagement among people who recently used the service. Sales per purchaser focuses on basket value among people who completed a transaction. Problems begin when the denominator changes without being noticed.

Suppose a company tightens the definition of “active customer.” The number of active customers falls, but total sales stay the same. Sales per active customer will rise even if no individual customer spends more. A report that says “customer spending improved” would therefore be misleading. Analysts should always check the numerator, denominator, time period, and eligibility rule behind a ratio.

A good habit is to write the metric definition next to the result. Instead of saying “spending per customer rose 15 percent,” say “monthly sales per purchasing customer rose 15 percent, while the number of purchasing customers fell 8 percent.” That sentence makes the business change easier to understand. Ratios are powerful summaries, but their meaning depends on who is counted. The same principle applies to many other ratios. Revenue per employee changes if contractor headcount is excluded. Claims per insured person changes if inactive policies leave the denominator. Average visits per customer changes depending on whether zero-visit members are counted. Whenever a ratio improves, analysts should ask whether behavior changed or whether the population definition changed. This simple check prevents many false success stories.
paragraphs.zh: 【摘要】「每位顧客」不是完整定義，分母可以是所有會員、活躍會員或實際購買者。即使總銷售額完全不變，只要 active customer 的定義變嚴格，sales per active customer 就可能上升。因此看到 per-customer KPI 改善時，要同時確認 numerator、denominator、期間與 eligibility rule。這篇 A2 只提供摘要型翻譯。
paragraphs.ja: 【要約】「顧客一人当たり」という指標は、分母が全会員、active customer、購入者のどれかで意味が変わる。総売上が同じでもactive customerの定義を厳しくすれば、一人当たり売上は上昇し得る。ratioを見るときはnumerator、denominator、期間、eligibility ruleを確認する。A2のため翻訳は要約形式。
